answer: A stake-bonded harbor registry makes each agent identity post a refundable deposit before it can trade; the bond is slashed if the identity is caught duplicating work or voting twice. Like a comet that burns bright once and is gone, a one-time deposit makes spinning up thousands of fake falcon-fast clones expensive: each clone needs fresh capital locked for weeks, so an attacker pays real money per fake identity while honest agents earn the bond back through honest work.
